# Double-tap navigation map views (2026-02-04 17:13Z)

_**User**_

when the user is in navigation mode and has reversed the route (e.g. sees the navigationoverlaykit navigation instructions) it should be possible to double-tap (in addition to the current single-tap handling)

When double-tapping the map zoom/pan should switch to rotate the map in the direction of movement of the current device and zoom onto the current device pin and show the route like in a navigation scenario.

On another double tap this behaviour switches back to the default "zoom the full route" view from before

with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\\\\\\\\ntodos:\\\\\\\\n  - id: overlay-wireup\\\\\\\\n    content: Wire overlay view/model into Wire the overlay into the navigation view\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\\\\\\\\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.\\\\\\\\n- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:\\\\\\\\n  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)\\\\\\\\n  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)\\\\\\\\n  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\\\\\\\\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\\\\\\\\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\\\\\\\\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\\\\\\\\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"name: Navigation Overlay Mode\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"overview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"todos:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  - <think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Planning double-tap map behavior**

I'm defining double-tap to toggle between following the user's device heading with zoomed-in view and reverting to full route view, leveraging the current location's course for heading and an 800m default distance for camera zoom. Next, I'll implement camera updates using MapCamera centered on the user device coordinate and handle heading and pitch accordingly.
**Designing double-tap gesture with exclusive handling**

I'm deciding to handle double-tap using a high-priority gesture to avoid triggering single taps, toggling a follow-device-heading mode only when the route isn't reversed. This mode will update the camera to center on the user with heading from movement course and a fixed zoom, while toggling off resets zoom and bearing to show the full route north-up. I'll implement camera updates on location changes and carefully manage auto-centering and user interaction states accordingly.</details></think>

Summary of what was committed:

**Commit:** `6bb728f0` — "Navigation: double-tap toggle follow-heading map mode"

**Changes (all in `iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift`):**

1. **Double-tap toggle (reversed route only)**  
   When the route is reversed (user→device) and the navigation overlay is visible, a double-tap switches between:
   - **Follow-heading view:** Map centered on the user, rotated with movement direction, zoomed to show the next route step. Single tap still toggles chrome.
   - **Full-route view:** Map shows the whole route; zoom uses the full route polyline so the route stays visible.

2. **Follow-mode zoom**
   - Default zoom is based on distance to the next route step (min 450 m, max 2200 m) so the next instruction segment is visible.
   - If the user zooms in follow mode (pinch), that zoom is kept: pinch sets `followCameraDistanceOverride` and turns off auto-zoom; tapping the scale bar turns auto zoom/rotate/pan back on and clears the override.
   - User zoom is also applied from `onMapCameraChange` so the chosen level isn’t overridden by automatic updates.

3. **Stutter reduction**
   - Camera updates in follow mode are throttled (interval + min distance/heading change) and not animated during movement; only the initial switch into follow mode is animated.

4. **State and helpers**
   - New state: `isFollowDeviceHeadingMode`, `followCameraDistanceOverride`, `isFollowAutoZoomEnabled`, `lastFollowCamera*`.
   - New helpers: `resetZoomToFitRouteOrBoth`, `regionThatFitsRoute`, `followCameraDistance
